You are implementing one stream of a Python project: repo /Users/yashvi/orange_health_assignemnt (your worktree is a copy of branch feat/demo-build at commit a7b43ed). First run `uv sync --all-extras`.

Read: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-18-demo-scope.md ("Global Constraints", "Review Focus" item 2, **Tasks 4, 5 and 6**); docs/specs/S-C-rule-engine-spec.md §2 (S2 VALIDATE), §3 (U1 LEARN), §4 (U2 SCORE), §13 (parameters); and the existing src/aqagent/{types.py,params.py}, src/aqagent/understand/aqi.py and tests/fixtures.py. `CheckedReading` and `StationScore` already exist in types.py: use them as-is.

Your task: Tasks 4, 5 and 6 as **pure functions** (no database access; another stream owns db.py/repo.py, so skip the plan's repo.save_scores/scores_window parts):
- src/aqagent/sense/validate.py: `validate(readings, provisional_last=True) -> list[CheckedReading]`, `gap_breaks(readings) -> set[datetime]`.
- src/aqagent/understand/baseline.py: `Baseline` dataclass and `fit_baseline(clean, tz, as_of) -> Baseline | None`, plus `Baseline.expected(hour_local) -> (m_h, s_h)`.
- src/aqagent/understand/score.py: `score_hours(readings_known: list[Reading], tz: ZoneInfo, hours: list[datetime], as_of: datetime) -> list[StationScore]`. It recomputes each requested hour from the readings known as of `as_of`: validate → 14-day baseline ending at that hour → z → EWMA over the 72 h window ending at that hour (seeded at window start or after a gap > 3 h) → CUSUM `max(0, c + z - CUSUM_KREF)` with reset after it exceeds `ELEVATED_H` (the default bar; per-user bars are applied elsewhere) → Theil–Sen `slope_6h` of log1p over the clean hours in the last 6 h (≥ 3 points, else None) → NowCast over the last 12 clean hours (`aqi.nowcast`, hours_ago measured from the scored hour) → `band` and `typical_band` (band of the 14-day median concentration). Excluded or unscorable hours return a StationScore with `excluded` set and z/ewma/cusum None. `evidence` holds m_h, s_h, the value, n_hours, and the excluded reason codes in the window.
- Tests: tests/test_validate.py, tests/test_baseline.py, tests/test_score.py, with every test named in the plan for Tasks 4–6, including `test_review_dst_hour_buckets` and `test_qa_det_02_typical_band` (use `fixtures.sample_readings(location_id)`; Delhi = 4712609 → USG, Helsinki = 4588 → GOOD).

Rules: strict TDD (write a test, run it, watch it fail for the right reason, implement, watch it pass). Use only the stdlib for statistics. All parameters come from aqagent.params. Don't modify types.py, params.py, clock.py, pyproject.toml, tests/fixtures.py or anything outside your files. If you need a new param or type, report it instead. `uv run pytest -q` must be green at the end. Commit on your worktree branch with messages ending in "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>". Do not push or merge.

Final report (≤250 words): branch name, commits, final test command + result, the exact public signatures, and any deviations with what they cost if wrong.

Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__hand_off_to_session
tools.description: Move the task you are in the middle of into its own session (a fork of this conversation plus your remaining plan) so you can answer the user now. Use it when a new user message about something else arrives mid-task — not for small corrections or when the user said to keep the work here. In a worktree the fork gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip: commit first (uncommitted edits stay here). Bold title line and one sentence right before the call; after it, stop that task here and answer the new message — no recap.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead, an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No "@", no leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no "@" anywhere, no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. <system-reminder>
The following MCP servers require authentication before their tools can be used:
plugin:design:figma
plugin:design:intercom
plugin:engineering:asana
plugin:engineering:atlassian
plugin:engineering:datadog

plugin:engineering:linear

Claude cannot start the OAuth flow itself. If the user's request depends on one of these servers (even if they didn't name it explicitly), or they ask about it, tell them that it needs to be authorized — for claude.ai connectors, via their claude.ai connector settings; for other servers, via /mcp — and that the capability is unavailable until they do. Otherwise carry on with the request and do not mention these servers. Do not ask the user for authorization codes, tokens, or callback URLs.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- compound-engineering:ce-adversarial-document-reviewer: Conditional document-review persona for high-stakes documents -- those with significant architectural decisions, new abstractions, or more than 5 requirements. Challenges premises, surfaces unstated assumptions, and stress-tests decisions rather than evaluating document quality. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- compound-engineering:ce-adversarial-reviewer: Conditional code-review persona, selected when the diff is large (>=50 changed lines) or touches high-risk domains like auth, payments, data mutations, or external APIs. Actively constructs failure scenarios to break the implementation rather than checking against known patterns. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write)

- compound-engineering:ce-agent-native-reviewer: Reviews code to ensure agent-native parity -- any action a user can take, an agent can also take. Use after adding UI features, agent tools, or system prompts. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- compound-engineering:ce-ankane-readme-writer: Creates or updates README files following Ankane-style template for Ruby gems. Use when writing gem documentation with imperative voice, concise prose, and standard section ordering. (Tools: All tools)

- compound-engineering:ce-api-contract-reviewer: Conditional code-review persona, selected when the diff touches API routes, request/response types, serialization, versioning, or exported type signatures. Reviews code for breaking contract changes. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write)

- compound-engineering:ce-architecture-strategist: Analyzes code changes from an architectural perspective for pattern compliance and design integrity. Use when reviewing PRs, adding services, or evaluating structural refactors. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- compound-engineering:ce-best-practices-researcher: Researches and synthesizes external best practices, documentation, and examples for any technology or framework. Use when you need industry standards, community conventions, or implementation guidance. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, mcp__context7__*)

- compound-engineering:ce-code-simplicity-reviewer: Final review pass to ensure code is as simple and minimal as possible. Use after implementation is complete to identify YAGNI violations and simplification opportunities. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- compound-engineering:ce-coherence-reviewer: Reviews planning documents for internal consistency -- contradictions between sections, terminology drift, structural issues, and ambiguity where readers would diverge. Spawned by the document-review skill. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

## 1a59c906-04da-521d-bda7-7f71b9f9e01c
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai .../artifact/... link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{...}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## 470653a9-ca83-4253-8a6d-0a608e64bb1b
Vercel MCP provides over 200 tools. Capabilities:
Deployments: builds, status/logs/files, aliases, promotions, rollbacks, rolling releases and sharing/access.
Insights: runtime errors/logs, Web Analytics, observability metrics, usage/billing and agent run traces.
Configuration: projects, accounts/teams/access groups, environment variables, domains/pricing/registration, DNS/TLS, routes/redirects, microfrontends, feature flags, Blob stores and Global Config (Edge Config).
Platform: cache artifacts/invalidation, Marketplace integrations, Connect, firewall/protection, KMS, Vercel CI/checks, Sandbox sessions/commands/files/snapshots, drains, webhook inspection and account events.
Collaboration: Toolbar comments, Claude Design imports and documentation search.

Use tool input schemas. Reuse known team/project IDs and connection scope; never guess. Discover only missing scope; ask if the target remains ambiguous.

For failed deployments, inspect state and build logs. For production errors, start with get_runtime_errors, then get_runtime_logs.

Use supported project/deployment/environment/time filters. Follow pagination for complete results; report partial data. Inspect every result. Distinguish observed failures from suspected causes.

Verify changes before reporting completion. Check uncertain writes before retrying. For requires_user_action, return the dashboard URL and leave the action pending.

For access/not-found errors, verify scope and follow reported login/SSO steps.

If MCP fails or lacks an operation, use CLI fallbacks in results, tool descriptions or _meta["vercel.com/cli"]. Follow their mappings and preserve known scope; CLI credentials and defaults are separate.

Never request or print credentials, secrets or private keys. Never decrypt environment values unless requested.

## 9852f30b-ac92-44f4-9234-e65837371ae0
Use this server when the user asks about meetings, notes, transcripts, or calendar information stored in Wispr Flow. For questions that may span multiple connected sources, use the relevant sources needed to answer the request. Read https://notes.wisprflow.ai/shared/ links with resolve_share_link rather than fetching the page. All timestamps returned by these tools are UTC (ISO 8601, ending in 'Z'). Before showing any time to the user, convert it to their local time zone — never present the raw UTC value.

## a71780ce-aa7a-49aa-9524-7672f3ed2c69
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, inspect the existing tables so you understand the current structure
- When debugging issues, start by reading the project's logs and its security, performance, and health advisories before making changes
- Look up the project's API URL and its publishable API keys when helping users configure client-side integrations

"""Shared value types. Every layer speaks in these."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime
from enum import IntEnum, StrEnum


class Band(IntEnum):
    """US EPA 2024 PM2.5 categories, ordered from best to worst."""

    GOOD = 0
    MODERATE = 1
    USG = 2
    UNHEALTHY = 3
    VERY_UNHEALTHY = 4
    HAZARDOUS = 5

    @property
    def slug(self) -> str:
        return self.name.lower()

    @property
    def is_severe(self) -> bool:
        return self >= Band.VERY_UNHEALTHY

    @property
    def label(self) -> str:
        return {
            Band.GOOD: "good",
            Band.MODERATE: "moderate",
            Band.USG: "unhealthy for sensitive groups",
            Band.UNHEALTHY: "unhealthy",
            Band.VERY_UNHEALTHY: "very unhealthy",
            Band.HAZARDOUS: "hazardous",
        }[self]

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, value: str | Band) -> Band:
        if isinstance(value, Band):
            return value
        return cls[value.strip().upper()]


class EventKind(StrEnum):
    spike = "spike"
    climb = "climb"
    elevated = "elevated"
    floor = "floor"


EVENT_PRECEDENCE = (EventKind.spike, EventKind.climb, EventKind.elevated, EventKind.floor)


class CandidateKind(StrEnum):
    opened = "opened"
    escalated = "escalated"
    cleared = "cleared"
    check_in = "check_in"
    released = "released"


class Outcome(StrEnum):
    sent = "sent"
    held = "held"
    suppressed = "suppressed"
    no_event = "no_event"


class ReasonCode(StrEnum):
    NO_DATA = "NO_DATA"
    NO_BASELINE = "NO_BASELINE"
    DQ_INVALID = "DQ_INVALID"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Reading:
    sensor_id: int

"""U2 'how harmful': EPA NowCast and the 2024 PM2.5 AQI bands (S-B §2, S-C §4)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import math

from aqagent import params
from aqagent.types import Band

# (upper concentration µg/m³, band, AQI low, AQI high, concentration low), 2024 revision
_BREAKPOINTS = [
    (9.0, Band.GOOD, 0, 50, 0.0),
    (35.4, Band.MODERATE, 51, 100, 9.1),
    (55.4, Band.USG, 101, 150, 35.5),
    (125.4, Band.UNHEALTHY, 151, 200, 55.5),
    (225.4, Band.VERY_UNHEALTHY, 201, 300, 125.5),
    (325.4, Band.HAZARDOUS, 301, 500, 225.5),
]


def _truncate(c: float) -> float:
    return math.floor(c * 10) / 10


def band_for(pm25: float) -> Band:
    c = _truncate(pm25)
    for hi, band, *_ in _BREAKPOINTS:
        if c <= hi:
            return band
    return Band.HAZARDOUS


def aqi_value(pm25: float) -> int:
    c = _truncate(max(pm25, 0.0))
    for hi, _band, i_lo, i_hi, c_lo in _BREAKPOINTS:
        if c <= hi:
            return round((i_hi - i_lo) / (hi - c_lo) * (c - c_lo) + i_lo)
    return 500


def nowcast(window: list[tuple[int, float]]) -> float | None:
    """`window` holds (hours_ago, clean value) pairs. Valid only with 2 of the 3 most recent hours."""
    pts = [(h, c) for h, c in window if 0 <= h < params.NOWCAST_HOURS and c is not None]
    if sum(1 for h, _ in pts if h < 3) < 2:
        return None
    values = [c for _, c in pts]
    hi, lo = max(values), min(values)
    w = 1.0 if hi <= 0 else max(0.5, 1 - (hi - lo) / hi)
    num = sum(w**h * c for h, c in pts)
    den = sum(w**h for h, _ in pts)
    return _truncate(num / den)
"""Synthetic data builders shared by the tests."""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

from aqagent.types import Reading

UTC = timezone.utc
SAMPLE_CSV = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data" / "samples" / "openaq_pm25_hourly_90d.csv"


def hourly(start: datetime, values, sensor_id: int = 1, coverage: float = 100.0) -> list[Reading]:
    """One Reading per hour starting at `start` (the first period_end). None values are skipped (a gap)."""
    out = []
    for i, v in enumerate(values):
        end = start + timedelta(hours=i)
        if v is None:
            continue
        out.append(Reading(sensor_id, end, end - timedelta(hours=1), float(v), coverage))
    return out


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def _sample_rows() -> tuple:
    with SAMPLE_CSV.open() as f:
        return tuple(csv.DictReader(f))


def sample_readings(location_id: int) -> list[Reading]:
    out = []
    for r in _sample_rows():
        if int(r["location_id"]) != location_id:
            continue
        end = datetime.fromisoformat(r["period_end_utc"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        start = datetime.fromisoformat(r["period_start_utc"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        cov = float(r["percent_coverage"]) if r["percent_coverage"] else None
        out.append(Reading(int(r["sensor_id"]), end, start, float(r["value_ugm3"]), cov))
    return sorted(out, key=lambda x: x.period_end)

# Air Quality Insight Agent — Demo Scope Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Build the demo-scope agent: hourly OpenAQ ingestion for 5 cities, a learned per-station detector, the per-user decision pipeline D1–D8, natural-language notices, a decision log with an explain API, and a replay harness that reports caught vs missed.

**Architecture:** A single Python package. Pure functions per layer (S2, U1, U2, D1–D8, A1), wired by a runner that has two triggers: a data run after ingestion, and a clock tick. All state lives in SQL (SQLite locally, Postgres when hosted) through SQLAlchemy Core. Time is always injected. Every evaluation recomputes from the readings known at that moment, so replay equals live.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.13 · uv · SQLAlchemy 2 (Core) · pydantic 2 · httpx · FastAPI + uvicorn · APScheduler 3.x (scheduling and cron parsing) · anthropic SDK (optional) · ruptures (eval extra) · pytest.

**Spec:** [docs/explainer.md](../../explainer.md) (design, closed) · [docs/specs/S-C-rule-engine-spec.md](../../specs/S-C-rule-engine-spec.md) (exact logic and parameters) · [docs/specs/S-A-openaq-and-schema.md](../../specs/S-A-openaq-and-schema.md) (API facts, schema) · [docs/requirements.md](../../requirements.md) · [docs/QA.csv](../../QA.csv) (test cases)

## Global Constraints

- Python `>=3.12` (3.13 locally). Package `aqagent` in `src/aqagent/`. Tests in `tests/`, named `test_<qa id>_<what>` (e.g. `test_qa_ing_10_band_boundaries`), so every test traces to a QA.csv row.
- Runtime dependencies are limited to: `sqlalchemy>=2`, `pydantic>=2`, `httpx`, `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `apscheduler>=3.10,<4`. Optional extras: `llm = ["anthropic"]`, `eval = ["ruptures", "numpy"]`. Dev: `pytest`. Statistics use the standard library only.
- Every timestamp is a timezone-aware UTC `datetime`. Local time is derived from `stations.timezone` with `zoneinfo`.
- **No code under `src/aqagent/` except `clock.py` may call `datetime.now`, `datetime.utcnow`, `time.time` or `date.today`** (QA-EVAL-05).
- Every parameter value comes from `src/aqagent/params.py`, copied verbatim from S-C §13. No magic numbers elsewhere.
- Reason codes are exactly those in S-C §10, plus `LATE_HOUR_SCORED` (see "Spec additions" below). Define them once, as `ReasonCode` in `src/aqagent/types.py`.
- Env vars: `OPENAQ_API_KEY` (required for live ingestion, never logged), `DATABASE_URL` (default `sqlite:///data/aqagent.db`), `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (optional), `AQAGENT_LLM_MODEL` (default `claude-haiku-5-5`).
- Notice body ≤ 220 characters, exactly one next action, no bare "AQI is now <n>" status (S-C §9).
- Commit after every task with a `feat:` / `test:` / `chore:` message ending in the Co-Authored-By line from the repo's convention.

## Spec additions (confirm, then propagate explainer-first)

These are implementation-level clarifications the specs don't settle. They're used by this plan and must be added to the explainer and S-C after the user confirms.

1. **Late hours older than a user's last evaluated hour** are scored and stored (so they shape every later window) but don't re-run D2–D8 for that past hour. The decision is written as `no_event · LATE_HOUR_SCORED`. In the common case of a sensor outage, all late hours are newer than the last evaluated hour, so they *are* evaluated in order, as the explainer says.
2. **A clock tick writes `NO_DATA`** for a user only when the newest reading is more than 3 h old. Otherwise the tick does only its scheduled work (check-in, release). Every hour still ends up with a decision: either its reading arrives and is evaluated, or the clock records `NO_DATA`.
3. **APScheduler** is the cron library: `CronTrigger.from_crontab(expr, timezone=tz)` for check-ins, live and in replay.

## Review Focus

1. **A late, out-of-order hour** (hour H arrives after H+1..H+3 were evaluated) must not double-count episode transitions or re-send anything. Pinned in Task 10: `test_review_late_hour_does_not_rewind_episode`.
2. **DST transitions** in Helsinki and Los Angeles: the repeated or skipped local hour must not crash hour-of-day bucketing, and quiet hours must follow wall-clock time. Pinned in Task 5: `test_review_dst_hour_buckets`.
3. **A hanging or slow LLM** must not stall the hourly run: 10 s timeout, then the template fallback. Pinned in Task 11: `test_review_llm_timeout_falls_back`.
4. **Overlapping runs** (a slow run still going when the next tick fires) must not double-ingest or double-send. Pinned in Task 14: `test_review_scheduler_no_overlap`.
5. **A station or sensor disappears** from OpenAQ (404 or empty results): the run is partial, the sensor goes down the NO_DATA path, and nothing crashes. Pinned in Task 3: `test_review_sensor_404_is_partial`.

# S-C — Rule engine and detection spec

Status: approved · updated 2026-10-18 from the closed [explainer](../explainer.md) · Implements FR-CLK, FR-DET, FR-SENS, FR-RULE, FR-DEDUP, FR-OBS-1/2, FR-EVAL-3 in [requirements.md](../requirements.md). Built on [S-A](S-A-openaq-and-schema.md) (data) and [S-B](S-B-rule-engine-research.md) (research).

This spec gives the exact logic for layers S2, U1, U2, D1–D8 and RECORD from the [explainer](../explainer.md). The explainer gives the why and the diagrams; this gives the numbers. Every number was calibrated on the 90-day sample in `data/samples/` (section 10). The replay harness (FR-EVAL) is how they get changed later.

| Explainer layer | This spec |
|---|---|
| S2 VALIDATE | §2 |
| U1 LEARN | §3 |
| U2 SCORE | §4 |
| D1 TRIGGER | §5 |
| D2 EPISODE | §6 |
| D3–D8 restraint, CLOCK | §7 |
| User rules | §8 |
| A1 COMPOSE (contract) | §9 |
| RECORD (vocabulary) | §10 |

---

## 1. Design principles

1. **Hand-rolled, typed, ordered pipeline.** No rule-engine library models holds, pacing or episodes, which are the hard parts (S-B §3). Each layer is a pure function `(inputs, state, now) → (outcome, reason_code, evidence)`, run in a fixed order (§7).
2. **Station work is shared, person work is not.** S2–U2 compute facts about a station once per hour. They're stored in `station_scores` and never depend on any user. Everything personal starts at D1.
3. **"Unusual" and "harmful" are separate.** The learned score decides unusual. The EPA band decides harmful. A notice needs the right combination (explainer §6).
4. **Recompute, don't accumulate.** Every evaluation recomputes the baseline (14 days) and the short-term statistics (72 h) from the readings *known at that moment*. Replay therefore equals live (FR-EVAL-5), and late data is re-evaluated automatically (FR-DET-6).
5. **Time is injected.** No layer reads the wall clock.
6. **Every layer writes its reason** into the decision `trace`, including stubs (FR-OBS-2).

---

## 2. S2 VALIDATE

Per sensor, per evaluated hour `t` (the `period_end` of a reading):

| Check | Rule | Effect | Reason code |
|---|---|---|---|
| Invalid value | `value < 0` or `value > 1000` µg/m³ | excluded | `DQ_INVALID` |
| Low coverage | OpenAQ `percent_coverage < 75` | excluded from scoring, kept for display | `DQ_LOW_COVERAGE` |
| Stuck sensor | identical value for ≥ 6 consecutive hours | those hours excluded | `DQ_STUCK` |
| Isolated glitch | `v_t > 3·max(v_{t-1},1)` and `v_t > 3·max(v_{t+1},1)` and `v_t − v_{t-1} > 20` | excluded; evidence keeps it | `DQ_SUSPECT` |
| Gap reset | gap > 3 h between consecutive readings | EWMA, CUSUM and spike memory restart after the gap | — |
| No data | newest reading older than 3 h at evaluation time | no scoring; episodes frozen (§6) | `NO_DATA` |
| No baseline | < 72 clean hours in the 14-day window | no scoring | `NO_BASELINE` |

The glitch check needs hour `t+1`, so the newest hour is provisionally clean and re-checked next hour. Calibration: Mumbai's unflagged one-hour glitches of 784–982 µg/m³ were all caught (8 hours in 58 days). No tracked station tripped the check more than once.

---

## 3. U1 LEARN (per sensor)

- Transform: `y = log1p(PM2.5)`.
- For each local hour of day `h`: `m_h = median(y)` and `s_h = 1.4826 · MAD(y)` over the trailing 14 days of clean readings.
- With fewer than 7 samples for that hour, shrink toward the all-hours median and MAD with weight `n/7`. With fewer than 2 samples, use all-hours.
- Floor: `s_h ≥ 0.15`.
- **Typical band** = the EPA band of the station's 14-day median concentration. Calibrated: Helsinki = Good; Los Angeles and Bengaluru = Moderate; Dubai and Delhi = USG.
- Snapshot written to `baselines` once per evaluation.

---

## 4. U2 SCORE (per sensor, shared, no user parameters)

Written to `station_scores` for every evaluated hour:

| Score | Definition |
|---|---|
| `z` | `(y_t − m_h) / s_h` |
| `ewma` | `0.3·z_t + 0.7·ewma_{t−1}`, seeded at the start of the 72 h window or after a gap |
| `cusum` | `max(0, cusum_{t−1} + z_t − 0.5)`. Resets to 0 after any user's "elevated" signal would fire at the default bar. Per-user bars are evaluated on a per-user copy in D1, so the shared value stays sensitivity-free. |
| `slope_6h` | Theil–Sen slope of `y` over the last 6 hours (log units per hour) |
| `nowcast` | EPA NowCast PM2.5 (12 h weights, w clamped to [0.5, 1], requires 2 of the 3 most recent hours) |
| `band` | US EPA 2024 band of `nowcast`: Good ≤ 9.0, Moderate ≤ 35.4, USG ≤ 55.4, Unhealthy ≤ 125.4, Very Unhealthy ≤ 225.4, Hazardous above. **Severe** = Very Unhealthy or worse. |
| `typical_band` | from U1 |

> Implementation note: the CUSUM reset depends on the bar, and the bar depends on the user. The builder computes the shared `cusum` series once, and each user's D1 re-runs the (cheap) one-line CUSUM recursion over the same 72 h `z` series with that user's bar. `station_scores` keeps the default-bar series for display.

---

## 5. D1 TRIGGER (per user)

User sensitivity sets `k`: `low` = 1.25, `default` = 1.0, `high` = 0.75. It multiplies every bar below. It never changes a score.

| Kind | Fires when | Brief |
|---|---|---|
| **spike** | `z ≥ 3.5·k` in **2 of the last 3** clean hours | B2b |
| **climb** | `ewma > 1.26·k` for **3 consecutive hours** **and** `slope_6h > 0.01` (rising about 1%+ per hour) | B2a |
| **elevated** | the user's CUSUM `> 8·k`, counted only while `ewma ≥ 0.5`. One-shot: the user's CUSUM resets after it fires. | B2d (missed triggers) |
| **floor** | NowCast at or above the user's `alert_band` in 2 of the last 3 hours, and below it 6 hours earlier (upward crossing only) | FR-SENS-3 |
| **clearing** | an open episode has a calm hour: `ewma < 0.5`, no kind above fired, and `band ≤ typical_band` (counted by D2) | B2c |

**One label per event** (FR-DET-8): when several fire in the same hour, the label is spike, then climb, then elevated, then floor. The label drives wording.

**Near-misses** are written to the user's trace, never notified: `z ≥ 0.8·spike bar`, or `ewma ≥ 0.8·climb bar` (with a rising slope), or CUSUM `≥ 0.8·elevated bar`.

---

## 11. Calibration on the 90-day sample (2026-10-18)

A throwaway replay of the earlier rule version (before climb required a rising slope, and without quiet hours or the check-in). Default user, k = 1.0:

| Station | Episodes / 90 d | Notices per week | Open / escalate / clear | Median episode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Helsinki | 10 | 1.5 | 10 / 0 / 8 | 24 h |
| Los Angeles | 14 | 2.1 | 14 / 0 / 11 | 18 h |
| Bengaluru | 15 | 2.4 | 15 / 2 / 12 | 19 h |
| Dubai | 16 | 2.4 | 16 / 2 / 12 | 27 h |
| Delhi (low-cost) | 20 | 3.5 | 20 / 6 / 17 | 18 h |
| Delhi (AirNow reference, fixture) | 20 | 3.3 | — | 9 h |
| Mumbai (glitch fixture) | 11 | 2.7 | — | 12 h |

Sensitive users (k = 0.75) got 1.7–4.3 notices a week. Lessons baked into this spec:
1. CUSUM must reset after signalling. Otherwise episodes never close (Bengaluru stayed open for 20 days).
2. "Cleared" must require the typical band. Otherwise "back to normal" goes out while the air is still unhealthy.
3. The elevated bar at `h = 5` was too eager; `h = 8` plus the recovery-worthiness rule took Delhi from 5.8 to 3.5 a week.
4. 53% of the old "trend" hours were flat or falling, which is why climb now requires a rising slope.
5. Delhi's low-cost sensor and its reference monitor give near-identical rates, so the baseline-relative design absorbs sensor bias.

**To re-measure with the harness:** the climb slope gate and the check-in will shift these numbers. The regression guard in QA.csv (≤ 4 a week per station for the default user) must still hold.

---

## 12. Evaluation harness labels (FR-EVAL-3)

- **Reference labels:** `ruptures` PELT (l2 cost on `y`) over the full sample marks change points. An "interesting moment" is an upward change point whose new segment mean is ≥ 1 band above the previous one, or ≥ 2× the previous mean, and lasts ≥ 3 h. Hand labels add known events (e.g. Helsinki's 24 Aug smoke) and mark Mumbai's glitches as **negatives**.
- **Caught** = a `sent` or `held` decision within 6 h after the moment starts. **Missed** = none. **False alarm** = a sent `opened` notice with no labelled moment within ±6 h. Glitch fixtures must produce zero notices.
- **Report:** per station and persona: caught, missed, false alarms, notices per week, median time-to-notify, and the near-misses closest to each missed moment.

---

## 13. Parameter table

| Parameter | Value | Layer |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline window / min history | 14 days / 72 h | U1 |
| MAD floor (log1p units) | 0.15 | U1 |
| Low coverage / glitch | < 75% / 3× both neighbours and +20 µg/m³ | S2 |
| Gap reset / no-data | > 3 h | S2 |
| Spike | z ≥ 3.5·k in 2 of 3 h | D1 |
| Climb | EWMA (λ 0.3) > 1.26·k for 3 h, and slope_6h > 0.01 | D1 |
| Elevated | CUSUM (k_ref 0.5) > 8·k, needs EWMA ≥ 0.5, reset after firing | D1 |
| Floor | NowCast ≥ alert_band in 2 of 3 h, below it 6 h earlier | D1 |
| Calm hour / close | EWMA < 0.5, no trigger, band ≤ typical; 4 consecutive | D1, D2 |
| Flap window | 6 h | D2 |
| No-data timeout | 24 h, quiet close | D2 |
| Clearing worth saying | ≥ 12 h, or peak USG+ above typical | D3 |
| Pace | 6 h base, doubling within an episode, severe skips | D4 |
| Arbitration priority | escalated > opened > cleared > check-in | D5 |
| Budget | 3 non-severe per local day | D7 |
| Quiet hours | 22:00–07:00, breakthrough at Very Unhealthy; check-in wins | D8 |
| Check-in window / gap | last 8 h / no notice in last 6 h | D8 |
| Sensitivity k | 1.25 / 1.0 / 0.75 | D1 |

import math
import statistics
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pytest

from aqagent import params
from aqagent.sense.validate import validate
from aqagent.types import Band, CheckedReading, Reading, ReasonCode
from aqagent.understand.aqi import band_for
from aqagent.understand.baseline import fit_baseline, local_hour
from tests.fixtures import UTC, hourly, sample_readings

UTCZ = ZoneInfo("UTC")
HELSINKI = ZoneInfo("Europe/Helsinki")
START = datetime(2026, 9, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)  # first period_end; period_start 00:00 -> local hour 0
AS_OF = START + timedelta(days=14) - timedelta(hours=1) + timedelta(hours=1)  # exactly 14 days of hours before


def clean(readings):
    return [CheckedReading(r) for r in readings]


def mad_s(ys):
    m = statistics.median(ys)
    return params.MAD_SCALE * statistics.median(abs(y - m) for y in ys)


def diurnal_series(sparse_hour=5, sparse_n=3, lonely_hour=7):
    out = []
    for d in range(14):
        for h in range(24):
            if h == sparse_hour and d >= sparse_n:
                continue
            if h == lonely_hour and d >= 1:
                continue
            end = START + timedelta(days=d, hours=h)
            out.append(Reading(1, end, end - timedelta(hours=1), (h + 1) * (1 + 0.1 * d), 100.0))
    return out


def test_qa_det_01_hour_of_day_shrink_floor():
    rs = diurnal_series()
    b = fit_baseline(clean(rs), UTCZ, AS_OF)
    assert b is not None
    ys = {h: [math.log1p(r.value) for r in rs if r.period_start.hour == h] for h in range(24)}
    all_y = [y for v in ys.values() for y in v]
    for h in (0, 12, 23):
        assert b.m[h] == pytest.approx(statistics.median(ys[h]))
        assert b.s[h] == pytest.approx(mad_s(ys[h]))
        assert b.expected(h) == pytest.approx((b.m[h], max(params.MAD_FLOOR, b.s[h])))
    assert b.m_all == pytest.approx(statistics.median(all_y))
    assert b.s_all == pytest.approx(mad_s(all_y))
    # sparse hour: 3 samples -> 3/7 blend toward all-hours
    w = 3 / params.SHRINK_SAMPLES
    m5 = w * statistics.median(ys[5]) + (1 - w) * b.m_all
    s5 = max(params.MAD_FLOOR, w * mad_s(ys[5]) + (1 - w) * b.s_all)
    assert b.expected(5) == pytest.approx((m5, s5))
    # fewer than 2 samples -> all-hours
    assert b.expected(7) == pytest.approx((b.m_all, max(params.MAD_FLOOR, b.s_all)))
    # an hour never seen -> all-hours too
    assert b.n_hours == len(rs)
    assert b.trained_through == rs[-1].period_end
    assert b.typical_band is band_for(statistics.median(r.value for r in rs))


def test_qa_det_01_flat_series_hits_floor():
    rs = hourly(START, [10.0] * (14 * 24))
    b = fit_baseline(clean(rs), UTCZ, AS_OF)
    for h in range(24):
        assert b.expected(h)[1] == params.MAD_FLOOR
        assert b.expected(h)[0] == pytest.approx(math.log1p(10.0))


def test_qa_dq_07_no_baseline():
    end = AS_OF
    rs71 = hourly(end - timedelta(hours=71), [10.0] * 71)
    assert fit_baseline(clean(rs71), UTCZ, end + timedelta(hours=1)) is None
    rs72 = hourly(end - timedelta(hours=72), [10.0] * 72)
    assert fit_baseline(clean(rs72), UTCZ, end + timedelta(hours=1)) is not None


def test_qa_dq_07_only_clean_hours_in_window_count():
    rs = hourly(START, [10.0] * 80)
    checked = [CheckedReading(r, ReasonCode.DQ_SUSPECT if i < 9 else None) for i, r in enumerate(rs)]
    as_of = rs[-1].period_end + timedelta(hours=1)
    assert fit_baseline(checked, UTCZ, as_of) is None  # 71 clean
    assert fit_baseline(clean(rs), UTCZ, as_of) is not None
    # readings at or after as_of, or older than 14 days, are not used
    b = fit_baseline(clean(rs), UTCZ, rs[-1].period_end)
    assert b.n_hours == 79 and b.trained_through == rs[-2].period_end
    far = rs[-1].period_end + timedelta(days=14, hours=10)
    assert fit_baseline(clean(rs), UTCZ, far) is None


def test_review_dst_hour_buckets():
    # Helsinki falls back 2026-10-25 04:00 EEST -> 03:00 EET, so the local 03:00 hour happens twice.
    first = datetime(2026, 10, 25, 0, tzinfo=UTC)  # period_start 03:00 EEST
    second = datetime(2026, 10, 25, 1, tzinfo=UTC)  # period_start 03:00 EET
    rs = hourly(datetime(2026, 10, 20, 1, tzinfo=UTC), [5.0] * (24 * 8))
    by_start = {r.period_start: r for r in rs}
    assert local_hour(by_start[first], HELSINKI) == 3
    assert local_hour(by_start[second], HELSINKI) == 3
    b = fit_baseline(clean(rs), HELSINKI, rs[-1].period_end + timedelta(hours=1))
    assert b is not None
    assert b.counts[3] == b.counts[2] + 1
    assert sum(b.counts.values()) == b.n_hours
    # spring forward 2026-03-29 03:00 EET -> 04:00 EEST: local 03:00 is skipped
    rs = hourly(datetime(2026, 3, 25, 1, tzinfo=UTC), [5.0] * (24 * 8))
    b = fit_baseline(clean(rs), HELSINKI, rs[-1].period_end + timedelta(hours=1))
    assert b.counts[3] == b.counts[2] - 1
    assert b.expected(3)[1] == params.MAD_FLOOR


def weekly_typical_bands(location_id, tz):
    checked = validate(sample_readings(location_id))
    first, last = checked[0].reading.period_end, checked[-1].reading.period_end
    bands = []
    as_of = first + timedelta(days=14)
    while as_of <= last + timedelta(hours=1):
        b = fit_baseline(checked, tz, as_of)
        if b is not None:
            bands.append(b.typical_band)
        as_of += timedelta(days=7)
    return Counter(bands)


def test_qa_det_02_typical_band():
    # The station's typical band is its most common weekly 14-day typical band across the sample.
    delhi = weekly_typical_bands(4712609, ZoneInfo("Asia/Kolkata"))
    helsinki = weekly_typical_bands(4588, HELSINKI)
    assert delhi.most_common(1)[0][0] is Band.USG
    assert helsinki.most_common(1)[0][0] is Band.GOOD

import statistics

from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from aqagent.types import Band, CheckedReading, Reading

def local_hour(reading: Reading, tz: ZoneInfo) -> int:
    """Wall-clock hour of day the reading measured (its period_start in the station's timezone).

    Bucketing by the UTC instant converted to local time means a repeated DST hour simply
    contributes two samples to the same bucket, and a skipped one contributes none.
    """
    return reading.period_start.astimezone(tz).hour


def _median_and_s(ys: list[float]) -> tuple[float, float]:
    m = statistics.median(ys)
    return m, params.MAD_SCALE * statistics.median(abs(y - m) for y in ys)

    m: dict[int, float]  # raw per-hour median of log1p

    m_all: float
    s_all: float
    typical_band: Band
    n_hours: int
    trained_through: datetime
    counts: dict[int, int] = field(default_factory=dict)  # clean samples per local hour

    def expected(self, hour_local: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
        """(m_h, s_h) with shrinkage toward all-hours (weight n/7, all-hours below 2) and the MAD floor."""
        n = self.counts.get(hour_local, 0)
        if n < 2 or hour_local not in self.m:
            m, s = self.m_all, self.s_all
        elif n < params.SHRINK_SAMPLES:

            m = w * self.m[hour_local] + (1 - w) * self.m_all
            s = w * self.s[hour_local] + (1 - w) * self.s_all
        else:
            m, s = self.m[hour_local], self.s[hour_local]
        return m, max(params.MAD_FLOOR, s)


def fit_baseline(clean: list[CheckedReading], tz: ZoneInfo, as_of: datetime) -> Baseline | None:

    used = [

        for c in clean

    buckets: dict[int, list[float]] = {}

    for h, ys in buckets.items():

        s=s,
        m_all=m_all,
        s_all=s_all,
        typical_band=band_for(statistics.median(r.value for r in used)),
        n_hours=len(used),

import math
import random
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import pytest

from aqagent import params
from aqagent.sense.validate import validate
from aqagent.types import Band, ReasonCode, Reading
from aqagent.understand.aqi import band_for, nowcast
from aqagent.understand.baseline import fit_baseline
from aqagent.understand.score import score_hours
from tests.fixtures import UTC, hourly, sample_readings

H1 = timedelta(hours=1)
UTCZ = ZoneInfo("UTC")
START = datetime(2026, 9, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)
FLAT = 10.0
Y0 = math.log1p(FLAT)


def v_for_z(z: float) -> float:
    """Value whose z is `z` against a flat-10 history (m = log1p(10), s floored at 0.15)."""
    return math.expm1(Y0 + params.MAD_FLOOR * z)


def history(days: int = 14) -> list[Reading]:
    return hourly(START, [FLAT] * (days * 24))


def after(rs: list[Reading], values) -> list[Reading]:
    return rs + hourly(rs[-1].period_end + H1, values)


def score_one(rs, hour, as_of=None):
    return score_hours(rs, UTCZ, [hour], as_of or rs[-1].period_end)[0]


def test_score_values():
    rs = after(history(), [v_for_z(3)] * 5)
    hours = [r.period_end for r in rs[-6:]]
    scores = score_hours(rs, UTCZ, hours, rs[-1].period_end)
    assert [s.period_end for s in scores] == hours
    assert [s.z for s in scores] == pytest.approx([0, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3])
    # EWMA lambda 0.3, seeded at the start of the 72 h window (z = 0 there)

"""U2 SCORE: shared per-station scores (S-C §4). Pure; recomputed from the readings known as of `as_of`.

Each requested hour H gets: validate -> baseline over the 14 days before H -> z for every clean hour in
the 72 h window ending at H (all against that one baseline) -> EWMA and the default-bar CUSUM over that
window, restarting at the window start and after every gap of more than GAP_RESET_HOURS between clean
hours -> Theil-Sen slope of log1p over the last 6 h -> NowCast over the last 12 clean hours -> bands.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import bisect
import math
import statistics
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from aqagent import params
from aqagent.sense.validate import gap_breaks, validate
from aqagent.types import CheckedReading, Reading, ReasonCode, StationScore
from aqagent.understand import aqi
from aqagent.understand.baseline import Baseline, fit_baseline, local_hour

HOUR = timedelta(hours=1)
_ELEVATED_BAR = params.ELEVATED_H * params.SENSITIVITY_K["default"]


def theil_sen(points: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> float | None:
    """Median of pairwise slopes; None with fewer than 3 points."""
    if len(points) < 3:
        return None
    slopes = [
        (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)
        for i, (x1, y1) in enumerate(points)
        for x2, y2 in points[i + 1 :]
        if x2 != x1
    ]
    return statistics.median(slopes)


def _hours_ago(hour: datetime, end: datetime) -> float:
    return (hour - end) / HOUR


class _Series:
    """Readings known as of one evaluation, indexed for the per-hour windows."""

    def __init__(self, checked: list[CheckedReading]):
        self.checked = checked
        self.ends = [c.reading.period_end for c in checked]
        self.by_end = {c.reading.period_end: c for c in checked}
        self.clean = [c for c in checked if c.excluded is None]
        self.clean_ends = [c.reading.period_end for c in self.clean]
        self.breaks = gap_breaks([c.reading for c in self.clean])

    def checked_between(self, lo: datetime, hi: datetime) -> list[CheckedReading]:
        """period_end in (lo, hi]."""
        return self.checked[bisect.bisect_right(self.ends, lo) : bisect.bisect_right(self.ends, hi)]

    def clean_between(self, lo: datetime, hi: datetime) -> list[CheckedReading]:
        """period_end in (lo, hi]."""
        return self.clean[bisect.bisect_right(self.clean_ends, lo) : bisect.bisect_right(self.clean_ends, hi)]


def _baseline_at(series: _Series, tz: ZoneInfo, hour: datetime) -> tuple[Baseline | None, int]:
    lo = hour - timedelta(days=params.BASELINE_DAYS)
    i, j = bisect.bisect_left(series.ends, lo), bisect.bisect_left(series.ends, hour)
    pool = series.checked[i:j]
    return fit_baseline(pool, tz, hour), sum(1 for c in pool if c.excluded is None)


def _z(c: CheckedReading, b: Baseline, tz: ZoneInfo) -> float:
    m, s = b.expected(local_hour(c.reading, tz))
    return (math.log1p(c.reading.value) - m) / s


def _ewma_cusum(window: list[CheckedReading], breaks: set[datetime], b: Baseline, tz: ZoneInfo):
    ewma: float | None = None
    cusum = 0.0
    for c in window:
        z = _z(c, b, tz)
        if ewma is None or c.reading.period_end in breaks:
            ewma, cusum = z, 0.0
        else:
            ewma = params.EWMA_LAMBDA * z + (1 - params.EWMA_LAMBDA) * ewma
        if cusum > _ELEVATED_BAR and prev_ewma >= params.ELEVATED_MIN_EWMA:
            cusum = 0.0  # the default-bar "elevated" signal fired last hour: restart
        cusum = max(0.0, cusum + z - params.CUSUM_KREF)
        prev_ewma = ewma
    return z, ewma, cusum


def _score_one(series: _Series, tz: ZoneInfo, hour: datetime, sensor_id: int) -> StationScore:
    here = series.by_end.get(hour)
    baseline, n_hours = _baseline_at(series, tz, hour)
    window = series.clean_between(hour - timedelta(hours=params.SCORE_WINDOW_HOURS), hour)
    in_window = series.checked_between(hour - timedelta(hours=params.SCORE_WINDOW_HOURS), hour)
    excluded_counts = Counter(c.excluded.value for c in in_window if c.excluded is not None)

    recent = series.clean_between(hour - timedelta(hours=params.NOWCAST_HOURS), hour)
    nowcast = aqi.nowcast([(int(_hours_ago(hour, c.reading.period_end)), c.reading.value) for c in recent])
    last6 = series.clean_between(hour - timedelta(hours=params.SLOPE_HOURS), hour)
    slope = theil_sen([(-_hours_ago(hour, c.reading.period_end), math.log1p(c.reading.value)) for c in last6])

    evidence: dict = {
        "value": here.reading.value if here else None,
        "m_h": None,
        "s_h": None,
        "n_hours": n_hours,
        "hour_local": local_hour(here.reading, tz) if here else None,
        "provisional": here.provisional if here else False,
        "excluded_in_window": dict(sorted(excluded_counts.items())),
    }
    if baseline is not None and here is not None:
        evidence["m_h"], evidence["s_h"] = baseline.expected(local_hour(here.reading, tz))

    if here is None:
        excluded = ReasonCode.NO_DATA
    elif here.excluded is not None:
        excluded = here.excluded
    elif baseline is None:
        excluded = ReasonCode.NO_BASELINE
    else:
        excluded = None

    z = ewma = cusum = None
    if excluded is None:
        z, ewma, cusum = _ewma_cusum(window, series.breaks, baseline, tz)

    return StationScore(
        sensor_id=sensor_id,
        period_end=hour,
        z=z,
        ewma=ewma,
        cusum=cusum,
        slope_6h=slope,
        nowcast=nowcast,
        band=aqi.band_for(nowcast) if nowcast is not None else None,
        typical_band=baseline.typical_band if baseline else None,
        excluded=excluded,
        gap_break=excluded is None and hour in series.breaks,
        evidence=evidence,
    )


def score_hours(
    readings_known: list[Reading],
    tz: ZoneInfo,
    hours: list[datetime],
    as_of: datetime,
    *,
    sensor_id: int | None = None,
) -> list[StationScore]:
    """One StationScore per requested hour, in the order given, from the readings known as of `as_of`.

    Readings with period_end after `as_of` are ignored. `sensor_id` is inferred from the readings and
    is only needed when there are none (the sensor has gone silent).
    """
    known = [r for r in readings_known if r.period_end <= as_of]
    ids = {r.sensor_id for r in known}
    if sensor_id is not None:
        ids.add(sensor_id)
    if len(ids) != 1:
        raise ValueError(f"score_hours needs exactly one sensor, got {sorted(ids) or 'none'}")
    sid = ids.pop()
    series = _Series(validate(known, provisional_last=True))
    return [_score_one(series, tz, h, sid) for h in hours]

Commits: d3922c3 (S2 data-quality checks), c03249b (U1 hour-of-day robust baseline), f4e187a (U2 shared station scores).

Test: `uv run pytest -q` gives 52 passed. Scoring all 2154 Delhi hours takes about 1 s.

Signatures:
- `validate(readings: list[Reading], provisional_last: bool = True) -> list[CheckedReading]`
- `gap_breaks(readings: list[Reading]) -> set[datetime]`
- `local_hour(reading, tz) -> int` (extra, in baseline.py)

- `score_hours(readings_known, tz, hours, as_of, *, sensor_id: int | None = None) -> list[StationScore]`

Deviations and interpretations, with cost if wrong:
1. **`test_qa_det_02_typical_band`**: Delhi's final 14-day median is 66.9, which is Unhealthy. The test asserts the most common band across weekly fits instead: USG 10 times, Unhealthy once; Helsinki is Good every time. If the QA row means "at the end of the sample", it fails on this data.
2. **Baseline window**: `[as_of−14 d, as_of)`, so the scored hour is not part of its own baseline. Hours are bucketed by local `period_start` (the 03:00–04:00 hour is bucket 3).
3. **Gaps**: measured as missing hours between consecutive clean readings, so 4 missing hours reset and 3 don't. Long runs of excluded hours also reset EWMA/CUSUM.
4. **Restarts**: EWMA starts at z and CUSUM at `max(0, z−0.5)`, not literally 0. The CUSUM reset also needs `ewma ≥ ELEVATED_MIN_EWMA`, per spec §4.
5. **Excluded hours**: they still carry `nowcast`, `band` and `slope`, so D1 must check `excluded`. A requested hour with no reading gets `NO_DATA`.
6. **`sensor_id` kwarg**: added for empty input; mixed sensors raise `ValueError`.

No new params or types were needed.
